clue.text: Bird and bats in the belfry

definitions.meaning: a bird known for laying its eggs in other birds' nests
an idiom for being crazy or eccentric

explanation.surface: A bird keeps company with the bats in a church tower.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the familiar European bird with a two-note call; the other is slang for mad, matching the idiom of bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Horses supplied by sergeant, possibly corralled by brothers

indicators.note: a corral pens animals in, so the brothers enclose the sergeant

parts.note: a sergeant is one example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: Some horses are provided by an army sergeant and penned in by a pair of brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Broncos are wild or half-broken horses of the American West, a species example of the general word.

clue.text: Plant poles in river

indicators.note: the poles are placed inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone has planted flagpoles in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Source of fruit to relieve poor

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fruit is grown in order to help the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree bears olives, so it is literally where that fruit comes from.

clue.text: Weight put on for show

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a gramme is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a broadcast show on television or radio.

clue.text: Lots turned on by goal

indicators.note: turned tells us to read the little word backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Plenty of excitement is switched on by a goal being scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a great many, an idiom for lots or loads.

clue.text: Olympian worries about disappearing

indicators.note: disappearing tells us the short word for about vanishes from the worries

parts.note: cares are worries
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete's anxieties about something fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares, Greek god of war, was one of the gods living on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Writing censored by editor put on trial

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a censored passage has been cut

explanation.surface: A writer whose work was censored by an editor ends up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute is to bring legal proceedings against someone, putting them on trial.

clue.text: Fruit crumble on a segment

indicators.note: to crumble is to break into pieces, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A fruit crumble topped with a single segment.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangosteen is a tropical fruit with sweet white segments.

clue.text: Violent criminals no good like this

indicators.note: no good says the letter for good is left out

parts.note: thugs are violent criminals

explanation.surface: Violent criminals are no good, as this shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is an adverb meaning in this way or like this.

clue.text: Irritable sailor returned empty trolley

indicators.note: returned says the word for sailor goes back to front

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, keeping just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A grumpy sailor brings back an empty trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: Unknown child removing the last of the Spanish wine

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for child is dropped

parts.note: an infant is a young child
del is Spanish for of the

explanation.surface: An unknown child leaves behind the last Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, mainly in California.

clue.text: Greek is after colour that's used in perfumery

indicators.note: Greek and is come after the colour

parts.note: amber is a yellowish-orange colour

explanation.surface: A Greek is chasing a colour used in making perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales, prized as a fixative in perfumes.

clue.text: Wood in which Napoleon gets English to advance

indicators.note: the letter for English moves forward towards the front

parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte

explanation.surface: In a forest Napoleon recruits English troops to push forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the E of BONEY to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard, very dark wood from tropical trees.

clue.text: Conductor, as separately entering railway system

indicators.note: entering means going into the word for the railway system
separately says the two letters of the word as are put in at different places

parts.note: a metro is an underground railway system
the word as is split, its first letter going in one spot and its second in another
the word as is split, its first letter going in one spot and its second in another

explanation.surface: A conductor travels separately on the underground.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes in after the M and S after the E, splitting AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Collective held back by cadet in Ukraine

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A collective group detained a military cadet in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together or acting jointly, as a collective does.

clue.text: Cop's malty brew that's found in cells

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A policeman's malty beer is discovered in the jail cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Cytoplasm is the material inside a living cell outside the nucleus.

clue.text: Turn a blind eye to trick that's performed

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
done means performed or carried out

explanation.surface: Someone overlooks a trick once it has been carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or accept wrongdoing, as one who ignores it does.

clue.text: Foolery involved large cast long ago

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Tomfoolery involving a big cast happened in the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' says L is thrown out of FOOLERY; the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned idiom meaning in times past.

clue.text: New wife for Irish saint

definitions.meaning: St ..., also called Brigid, is a patron saint of Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: A bride is a woman on her wedding day, and St Bride is the Irish saint Brigid of Kildare.

clue.text: Old French author penning one chapter is too fastidious

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the author surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Jules Verne was a French novelist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old French writer drafting a single chapter is excessively fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnice means excessively particular or fussy, the same as overly fastidious.

clue.text: Flower not yet replaced

definitions.meaning: read as flow-er, something that flows, like a stream of water

explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flow of water or air, a 'flower'; current also means present and still in use.

clue.text: Children skirting puddle initially step on it

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edge, so the children surround the letter

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or children

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word puddle

explanation.surface: Children avoiding a puddle are first to tread in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom for hurry up, so it means to speed.

clue.text: Soldier starts to relax on top bunk

parts.note: Tommy is a nickname for a British private soldier

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A soldier begins to relax on the top bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is informal for nonsense, and tommyrot is a British word for the same.

clue.text: Novelist, extremely strict, yielding least

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters of the word strict

explanation.surface: A very strict novelist gives very little ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The most stern person is the least willing to give way, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Detectives performed on show

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
played means performed, as a musician does

explanation.surface: Detectives performed in a public showcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed has been exhibited, put on show.

clue.text: Scriptures worthily translated

indicators.note: translated suggests changing the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Bible is rendered worthily into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is a term for sacred writings, especially the Bible.

clue.text: Eminent lord welcoming tax cut

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the lord surrounds the shortened tax

parts.note: a noble is a lord

indicators.note: cut means the tax word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A distinguished lord is happy to see taxes reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means distinguished or prominent, a synonym of eminent.

clue.text: Great uncertainty reported in retreat

indicators.note: reported says the phrase is as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: high means great, as in high hopes; doubt is uncertainty

explanation.surface: There is considerable doubt reported at a remote retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, somewhere one retreats to.

clue.text: On a vessel captain's first to yield to pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece on the others sits above them
first picks out the opening letter of captain's

parts.note: a vein is a blood vessel

explanation.surface: Aboard a ship, the captain is the first to crack under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is a phrasal idiom for giving way or submitting under pressure.

clue.text: Kingdom not fancied by leader of monarchists

parts.note: real is the opposite of fanciful or imagined

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of monarchists

explanation.surface: A kingdom that the head royalist doesn't favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Masked hero runs repeatedly through animal enclosure

indicators.note: through puts the runs inside the enclosure

parts.note: a zoo is a place where animals are kept

indicators.note: repeatedly means the run abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A masked hero dashes again and again through the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorro is the fictional masked swordsman of Spanish California.
